parts.title: Before Dawn
parts.text: Thandi's aunt, a wildlife photographer, drove Ingrid and Rafi onto the African **savanna** before sunrise. Golden grass rolled away in a vast **expanse**, broken only by a few flat-topped trees. They parked on a low hill, a perfect **vantage** point for watching the plain below. Her aunt draped the truck with a tan cloth so it looked **inconspicuous** against the dry grass.

parts.title: The Waiting Game
parts.text: "The best photographers are **unobtrusive**," her aunt whispered. "Animals should forget we are here." Rafi, who hated waiting, fidgeted until she explained that **patience** was the most important tool in her camera bag. For two hours they sat in perfect **stillness** while zebras grazed and a pair of eagles drifted overhead. Ingrid's legs went numb, but she did not complain.

parts.title: The Shot
parts.text: As dusk fell, **nocturnal** animals began to wake. Suddenly a serval, a long-legged spotted cat, began to **stalk** a field mouse through the tall grass, placing each paw with care. Ingrid's **instinct** told her to lift the camera before the cat moved. She rested her finger on the **shutter** and pressed so gently that it clicked only once. The moment was **fleeting**: a second later the mouse darted away and the cat sprang after it into the gloom.

parts.title: Back at Camp
parts.text: Around the fire, the three friends scrolled through the photographs. The sharpest one was not the best. Their favorite showed the cat frozen mid-step, one paw lifted. Thandi realized the picture existed only because they had given up talking, snacking and checking the time. Rafi announced that he wanted to wait the whole night next time, and everybody laughed, because they knew he meant it.

definitions.meaning1: Not easy to notice, because it blends in with its surroundings. Example: The gray moth was inconspicuous against the tree bark.
definitions.studentChallenge: Wearing green, the hiker was ___ among the leaves.

definitions.meaning1: To follow or approach a person or animal quietly and carefully, usually in order to hunt it. Example: The lioness began to stalk the herd through the tall grass.
definitions.meaning2: The main stem of a plant. Example: He snapped a stalk of celery in half.
definitions.studentChallenge: The cat crouched low to ___ the bird across the lawn.

definitions.meaning1: Active at night rather than during the day. Example: Owls are nocturnal birds that sleep through the day.
definitions.studentChallenge: Bats are ___ animals, so they hunt only after the sun goes down.

definitions.meaning1: A wide, open area of land, water, or sky. Example: A vast expanse of ice stretched in every direction.
definitions.studentChallenge: From the plane, we saw an endless ___ of blue ocean.

definitions.meaning1: A place or position that gives a good view. Example: The hill was a perfect vantage point for watching the parade.
definitions.meaning2: A particular way of looking at a situation. Example: From a teacher's vantage, the test results looked encouraging.
definitions.studentChallenge: From this high ___ point, we can see the whole valley.

definitions.meaning1: A natural feeling or way of behaving that you have without being taught. Example: A mother bird's instinct is to protect her eggs.
definitions.meaning2: A strong inner sense about something. Example: Her instinct told her something was wrong.
definitions.studentChallenge: Birds fly south each winter by ___, not because anyone taught them.

definitions.meaning1: The state of being quiet and not moving. Example: The stillness of the forest at dawn was peaceful.
definitions.studentChallenge: A sudden ___ fell over the room as the speaker raised her hand.

definitions.meaning1: The part of a camera that opens and closes to let light in. Example: The photographer pressed the shutter button halfway down.
definitions.meaning2: A hinged cover for a window. Example: She closed the shutter to keep the afternoon sun out.
definitions.studentChallenge: The camera's ___ clicked as the photographer took the picture.

definitions.meaning1: Not drawing attention to yourself; not getting in the way. Example: The waiter was so unobtrusive that we hardly noticed him refill our glasses.
definitions.studentChallenge: The photographer stayed ___ so the shy birds would not be scared away.

definitions.meaning1: A flat, grassy plain with few trees, found in warm parts of the world. Example: Elephants roamed across the African savanna.
definitions.studentChallenge: Lions and zebras live on the grassy ___ of Africa.

definitions.meaning1: The ability to wait calmly without getting upset. Example: Fishing takes patience, because the fish may not bite for hours.
definitions.meaning2: Calm, steady effort when something is difficult. Example: Learning the cello requires patience.
definitions.studentChallenge: It took great ___ to wait three hours for the bird to return.

definitions.meaning1: Lasting only a very short time. Example: She caught a fleeting glimpse of the fox before it vanished.
definitions.studentChallenge: The rainbow was ___, fading after only a minute.
